preregistered_claim.claim: bad (hand pose) frames concentrate near segment boundaries, i.e. the fraction of bad frames within +/-0.5 s of an interior segment boundary exceeds the duration-weighted base rate of those windows
preregistered_claim.base_rate_def: sum(clipped window length) / sum(record duration), all 38 records pooled
falsified_if: observed fraction < 1.5 x base rate, OR
the 95% CI of the fraction contains the base rate
preregistered_claim.known_limitation: bad frames occur in runs, so the binomial test over-states significance; a record-level (cluster) sign test and Wilcoxon signed-rank are reported alongside and are the conservative reading
secondary_analyses_declared: task-change boundaries only (boundary where segment description changes)

alignment_check.note: annotation_bad_frame_pose_hand.csv, pose_left_hand.csv and pose_right_hand.csv have identical row counts and identical _message_index sets; frame-for-frame alignment holds

composition.empty_reason_note: bad frames whose problem_type slots are all empty; total_bad_frames - resolvable

definition.tie_break: frames exactly on the boundary count as in-window (abs(t-b) <= w)
definition.pooling: all 38 records, frame-level dedup, duration-weighted base rate

reason_code_resolution.explanation: No numeric enum code appears in any problem_type[i] slot of the 38 records. The '1'/'2' values reported earlier are the problem_type.length column (number of problems on the row), not an enum code: rows with length=1 and length=2 sum to the 720 bad rows and int(length)==count(non-empty slots) for every bad row.

truncation_check.verdict: files without a problem_type[1] column never declare length>=2 on any bad row, so no reason string was dropped by the narrower schema

_derived_note: percentages derived from composition and boundary_vs_interior; nothing else in this file is modified
